{{Short description|Japanese-born American mathematician (1928–2026)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=January 2026}}
{{nihongo|'''Takashi Ono'''|小野 孝|Ono Takashi|18 December 1928 – 11 January 2026}} was a Japanese-born American mathematician, specializing in number theory and algebraic groups.

==Early life and education==
Ono was born in [[Nishinomiya]], Japan, on 18 December 1928. He received his Ph.D. in 1958 at [[Nagoya University]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=85974}}</ref>

==Career==
Ono immigrated to the United States after receiving an invitation from [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]] to work at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] with a fellowship for the two academic years from 1959 to 1961<ref name="IASRef">{{cite web| url= http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/5385| title= Ono, Takashi| publisher= [[Institute for Advanced Study]]| website= IAS.edu| date= 9 December 2019| access-date= | archive-date= 28 September 2015| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150928203254/https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/5385| url-status= live}}</ref> and then went to the [[University of British Columbia]] to work as an assistant professor of mathematics<ref>{{Cite web |title=Inauguration Address {{!}} Office of the President |url=https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |access-date=2023-03-08 |website=president.umich.edu |archive-date=2023-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230308005238/https://president.umich.edu/news-communications/speeches/inauguration-address/ |url-status=live }}</ref> from 1961 to 1964. From 1964 to 1969 Ono was a tenured professor at the [[University of Pennsylvania]]. From 1969 to his retirement in 2011, he was a professor at [[Johns Hopkins University]]. In 1966 he was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Moscow]].<ref name=IASRef/> In 2012 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web| url= http://hub.jhu.edu/2012/11/02/math-fellows-ams| title= 10 from JHU among inaugural fellows of American Mathematical Society| website= JHU.edu| publisher= [[Johns Hopkins University]]| date= 2 November 2012| access-date= | archive-date= 28 September 2015| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20150928220022/http://hub.jhu.edu/2012/11/02/math-fellows-ams| url-status= live}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Ono's youngest son, [[Ken Ono]], is also a mathematician<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.jsonline.com/news/wisconsin/29298744.html| url-status= dead |title= A flash of insight brings answers|last= Johnson| first= Mike| newspaper= [[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]] |date=13 March 2007| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20111112195129/http://www.jsonline.com/news/wisconsin/29298744.html| archive-date= November 12, 2011| access-date= August 24, 2017}}</ref> and professor at the [[University of Virginia]] as well as a former triathlete.<ref name= "Emory Ken">{{cite web| url= http://www.mathcs.emory.edu/~ono/about-me/| publisher= Department of Mathematics, [[Emory University]]| website= Emory.edu| title= About Me| first= Ken| last= Ono| access-date= August 24, 2017| archive-date= August 26, 2017| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170826125735/http://www.mathcs.emory.edu/~ono/about-me/| url-status= live}}</ref> His middle son, [[Santa J. Ono]], served as the 15th [[President of the University of Michigan]] (previously the President and Vice-Chancellor of the [[University of British Columbia]]) and is a biomedical researcher. His eldest son, Momoro Ono, is a music professor at [[Creighton University]].<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.creighton.edu/ccas/fineandperformingarts/degrees/music/musicfaculty/momoroono/ | title= Dr. Momoro Ono | publisher= Fine and Performing Arts, [[Creighton University]] | date=  | access-date= August 24, 2017 | website= Creighton.edu | archive-date= August 1, 2017 | archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170801121816/https://www.creighton.edu/ccas/fineandperformingarts/degrees/music/musicfaculty/momoroono/ | url-status= live }}</ref> Ono died on 11 January 2026, at the age of 97.<ref name=wallach>{{cite web |last=Wallach| first=Rachel| title =Acclaimed mathematician Takashi Ono dies at 97| url = https://hub.jhu.edu/2026/01/13/takashi-ono-obituary/| date = 2026-01-13}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* 1959: {{cite journal|title=On some arithmetic properties of linear algebraic groups|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]]| volume=70|issue=2|pages=266–290|jstor=1970104|doi=10.2307/1970104|last1=Ono|first1=Takashi|year=1959}}
* 1961: {{cite journal|title=Arithmetic of algebraic tori|journal=Annals of Mathematics| volume= 74 |pages= 101–139|jstor=1970307|doi=10.2307/1970307|last1=Ono|first1=Takashi|year=1961|issue=1}}
* 1963: {{cite journal|title=On the Tamagawa number of algebraic tori|journal=Annals of Mathematics |volume=7 8| pages= 47–73|jstor=1970502|doi=10.2307/1970502|last1=Ono |first1=Takashi |year=1963 |issue=1 }}
* 1964: {{cite journal|title=On the relative theory of Tamagawa numbers|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|year=1964|volume=70|issue=2|pages=325–326|mr=0156856|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1964-11140-x|doi-access=free|last1=Ono|first1=Takashi}}
* 1965: {{cite journal|title=On the relative theory of Tamagawa numbers|journal=Annals of Mathematics| volume= 82|pages=88–111|doi=10.2307/1970563|jstor=1970563|last1=Ono|first1=Takashi|year=1965|issue=1|url=http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.bams/1183525960}}
* 1965: {{cite journal|title=The Gauss-Bonnet theorem and the Tamagawa number|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|year=1965|volume=71|issue=2|pages=345–348|mr=0176986|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1965-11290-3|doi-access=free|last1=Ono|first1=Takashi}}
* 1969: {{cite journal|title=On Gaussian sums|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society |year=1969 |volume=75|pages=43–45|mr=0245547|doi=10.1090/s0002-9904-1969-12139-7|pmid=16590967|doi-access=free|last1=Ono |first1=Takashi |issue=7 |pmc=220918 }}
* 1969: {{cite journal|title=On algebraic groups and discontinuous groups|journal=Nagoya Mathematical Journal |year=1966 |volume= 27 |issue=Pt 1 |pages=279–322|doi=10.1017/S002776300001206X |url=https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.nmj/1118801634 |mr=0199193 |zbl=0166.29802|last1=Ono |first1=Takashi |doi-access=free }}
* 1990: {{cite book|title=An Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory|publisher=[[Plenum Publishers]]}}, {{cite book|title=2nd edition |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DoflBwAAQBAJ|isbn=9781461305736|last1 = Ono|first1 = Takashi|date = 6 December 2012| publisher=Springer }}
* 1994: {{cite book|title=Variations on a Theme of Euler: Quadratic Forms, Elliptic Curves and Hopf Maps|year=1994| publisher= Plenum|url=https://archive.org/details/variationsonthem0000onot |url-access=registration|isbn=9780306447891 }}
* 2008: {{cite book|title=Gauss sums and Poincaré sums|publisher= Nippon Hyoron Sha|language=ja}}
